item.text: {"text":"Search found related 2024–2026 work, but no verified exact match combining from-scratch character CNNs, numeric-unit composition and HSTU. [MARS (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00702) motivates attribute-aware representations and matching, but uses pretrained language models. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) combines BERT-derived item text with SASRec and includes reviews, making its full recipe unsuitable here. These papers support investigating structured text features; they do not establish gains for the permitted architecture and inputs.\n\nThe foundational [character-level CNN paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.01626) offers a suitable architectural precedent: learn ordered character-pattern detectors directly from text without pretrained word embeddings. A plausible HSTU experiment is a small randomly initialized character encoder over titles/descriptions, jointly trained through the recommendation loss and projected into the item representation. Convolutions capture local order; global pooling alone can discard broader arrangement, so connector direction may require wider receptive fields, positional pooling or a small position-aware token encoder. Preserve digits, decimal points, units and connector punctuation. [Tokenization Counts (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14903) shows numerical tokenization affects arithmetic performance, providing indirect motivation rather than recommendation evidence. Treat number-unit and direction discrimination as hypotheses to validate. Keep one jointly trained HSTU checkpoint per category, using the same learned item representation for history encoding and candidate scoring."}
